sources.title: Structured interview note containing the array reversal prompt
Tagged repository question record for array reversal
Deterministic Java validation against independent reverse-index mapping

claims.text: The recovered source says only array reversal and does not specify whether the input may be mutated, whether a new array is required, the element type, or null behavior; the candidate states those missing constraints instead of inventing them.
Under the explicitly chosen mutable-array contract, swapping symmetric positions with left and right pointers until left >= right produces the reverse order in place.

After each in-place swap, the newly consumed left and right positions equal their final reverse-index values, so the processed prefix and suffix remain correct while the unprocessed interval strictly shrinks.
When mutation is disallowed, a separate result array using result[i] = input[n-1-i] preserves the source array and returns the same reversed sequence.
Both variants inspect or place O(n) elements; the in-place variant uses O(1) additional space, while the copy variant uses O(n) result space.

Fixed cases and 5000 fixed-seed arrays match an independent reverse-index oracle; reversing in place twice restores the original array, the copy variant leaves its input unchanged, and the implementation's explicit null fail-fast choice is tested.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=7 randomized=5000 oracle=index-mapping involution=true null=fail-fast

boundary_tests.expected: center element remains at its reverse-mapped position

findings: The source boundary is preserved: the prompt is only array reversal, so mutation, output allocation, element type, and null handling are not falsely attributed to the interview source.
The candidate gives a directly usable in-place two-pointer solution and separately handles the non-mutating contract instead of conflating the two APIs.
The loop invariant establishes why each symmetric swap fixes two final positions and why odd-length centers need no action.
The validation oracle is based on independent reverse-index mapping rather than duplicating the swap implementation.
The reverse-twice involution check and copy-no-mutation check cover useful behavioral properties beyond example cases.
The null fail-fast behavior is explicitly labeled as an implementation decision outside the recovered source contract.
No project or production claims are fabricated.
Required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
